newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks at new high on Fed inaction.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks at new high on Fed inaction.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.345 +0.015 Gold NY 342.95 Lon fix 343.00
*No U.S. rate hike, Dow rise, boosts Australia stocks 0.5 pct to new record high. Firm copper buoys BHP. Volume 43.05 million, value A$87.59 million, 501 stocks traded, 199 steady, 224 up, 79 down.
Australian stocks powered to a new all-time high in early Wednesday trade as relief at no U.S. rate hike boosted the market overall and banks in particular.
Recovering from sharp weakness in recent days, banking stocks surged on revived talk that the banks will benefit from a low growth, low inflation economy.
"People are pretty happy about no rate hike in the U.S.," said Macquarie Equities broker Simon Jones.
The banks were strongest, but the strength was evident across the market, with the All Ordinaries Index rising 11.2 points to 2,541.9 in the first 10 minutes of trade.
This eclipsed the previous intra-day high of 2,540.4 set on the day the Australian budget was announced, May 13.
National Australia Bank led the banking stock rebound, rising 23 cents to A$18.03 and helping to drive the banking index up 50.1 points or 1.15 percent to 4,399.7.
"They've been sold off since the budget and for anyone looking to drive them back up, this is just what they were looking for," Macquarie's Jones said.
Resources giant BHP was also firmer, rising 11 cents to A$19.37 as investors welcomed news that copper prices rose to the key US$2,500 a tonne mark overnight.
This is the first day this week BHP and the big banks have moved in tandem, appearing to halt apparent switching from the banks to the resources groups.
Some profit-taking was seen however in RTZ Corp-CRA Ltd, which fell four cents to A$21.08 after its strong rise of earlier this week and in sympathy with RTZ shares in London.
Highlights amoung the smaller stocks included the 18 cent rise by whitegoods maker Email Ltd to A$4.06 after a five week strike at its Martin Bright steel plant ended.
Industrial services group Campbell Brothers rose 25 cents to A$4.90 after a strong profit result late on Tuesday.

Burns Philp & Co again fell nine cents to A$1.78 as investors voted with their feet over the food group's plan to sell off its spice assets in an attempt to restore profits. S&P put Burns Philp's ratings on negative watch late on Tuesday.
The appetite for shares in just-floated banc-assurance group Colonial Ltd appears yet to be exhausted, as it rose a further two cents to A$3.38 on volume of over two million.

Market interest is seen turning to de-regulated wage deal data for the March quarter due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), which is seen the key to the immediate outlook for local rates. An annual number over five percent would disappoint.

In other markets, the Australian dollar held to the US$0.7745 level, while local 10-year bond yields dipped three basis points to 7.63 percent in line with U.S. yields after the no-rate-hike decision.
